literature_notes: DLL4 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein (signal peptide 1–26, ectodomain 27–531, TM 532–552, intracellular 553–685). Both ledger lines describe C-terminal epitope tags on full-length membrane-anchored constructs. L1 (PMC10132381) explicitly fuses Myc and Flag tags to the C-terminus of the intracellular domain (after residue 685). L2 (PMC4482573) uses a reverse PCR primer encoding an HA tag, which by definition appends the tag at the coding-sequence C-terminus — also intracellular (after residue 685). Neither line reports any insertion on the extracellular face (residues 27–531), at the mature N-terminus (after residue 26), or in any extracellular loop. No ledger line supports an extracellular surface tag site; zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: Full-length membrane-anchored DLL4 construct carries C-terminal Myc (EQKLISEEDL) and Flag (DYKDDDDK) tags after the last intracellular residue V685; tags face the cytoplasm.
HA tag appended via reverse PCR primer to the C-terminus of full-length Dll4; for a type I TM protein this places the tag in the intracellular domain after residue 685.
